Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis and impressions: Prolonged fatigue with diffuse myalgias and decreased appetite after outdoor activity; evaluation prioritized for infectious etiologies (Lyme disease) with consideration of viral syndrome or autoimmune/endocrine causes based on DDx.
- Relevant differential diagnoses (aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Lyme disease (Lyme borreliosis) — High likelihood given calf-area rash, outdoor exposure, travel to the US, and systemic symptoms.
  - Viral infectious syndrome (e.g., EBV/CMV mononucleosis) — Moderate to high likelihood given prolonged fatigue and sore throat with brief fever.
  - Autoimmune/inflammatory conditions or autoimmune thyroiditis — Moderate likelihood given fatigue and joint/muscle aches with transient rash; warrants serology.
  - Endocrine/metabolic issues (hypothyroidism) or nutritional deficiencies (iron/B12) — Moderate likelihood; consider testing if symptoms persist or labs suggest abnormal results.
- Plan rationale: Blood work will assess organ function and hematologic status; Lyme serology will help confirm or exclude Lyme disease; results will guide treatment and further workup. If Lyme is positive, specific antibiotics would be initiated. Follow-up is planned about one week after testing (by phone) to review results.
- Management priorities: Obtain ordered labs; arrange Lyme serology; provide patient education about testing and potential treatments; schedule follow-up communication after results.

Management Plan

- Investigations ordered or recommended: CBC; liver function tests; kidney function tests; Lyme serology.
- Therapeutic actions: If Lyme serology is positive, initiate appropriate antibiotic therapy (as per standard Lyme treatment). No antibiotic therapy initiated at this time pending results.
- Follow-up and monitoring: Follow-up contact by phone approximately one week after tests to review results; additional in-person or telehealth follow-up as indicated.
- Patient education: Explain purpose of Lyme testing and broader infectious/medical evaluation; discuss potential need for further rheumatology or endocrine testing if results point toward autoimmune or metabolic conditions; advise to report new or worsening symptoms (fever, chest symptoms, neuro symptoms).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Lyme disease (Lyme borreliosis) — High
  - Justification: Calf rash with systemic symptoms after outdoor US exposure; fatigue for ~6 weeks; clinician planned Lyme serology and potential antibiotic treatment if positive.
  - Likelihood: High
- Viral/mononucleosis-like infectious syndrome (EBV/CMV) — Moderate to High
  - Justification: Prolonged fatigue with sore throat and brief fever; no focal organ symptoms.
  - Likelihood: Moderate-High
- Autoimmune/inflammatory disease or autoimmune thyroiditis — Moderate
  - Justification: Fatigue with multi-joint aches and transient rash could reflect autoimmune processes; would require serology.
  - Likelihood: Moderate
